<!-- gate-reference:start — generated by `go run ./tools/sitecli` from the gate catalog and the checker's spec; edit those, not this block -->

The layer a header declares is one the Estrutura has.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Checker | `header-layer-declared` |
| Confronts | `spec` `feature` `code` `test` |
| Blocking by default — new project | yes |
| Blocking by default — existing project | no — informs |

## How it measures

The header's `layer:` decides which templates derive the unit's siblings and where the
documentation files it. A layer the Estrutura does not have is read as nothing: the unit falls back
to the default templates, lands in a page of its own, and shows up — if at all — as a layer
outside every container on the architecture page. In the reference app a section declared
`layer: landing-component` for months while the Estrutura only had `landing-feature`, and it
surfaced by chance.

## Declaring it

```yaml
gates:
  - name: header-layer-declared
    on: [spec, feature, code, test]
    check: header-layer-declared
```
